GainsBlock.rationale: `public override bool GainsBlock => true` (EvilEye.cs:17) == the class attribute.

ctor.rationale: `base(1, CardType.Skill, CardRarity.Uncommon, TargetType.Self)` (EvilEye.cs:27-30) == cost 1 / SKILL / UNCOMMON / SELF. Evil Eye has NO Exhaust keyword of its own -- the Exhaust hover tip (EvilEye.cs:23) describes its TRIGGER -- and the sim leaves `exhausts` False.

CanonicalVars.rationale: `new BlockVar(8m, ValueProp.Move)` (EvilEye.cs:21) == `_block = 8`. Move without Unpowered -> POWERED block, so NOT in gap G1's blast radius.

OnPlay.rationale: `int blockGains = ((!WasCardExhaustedThisTurn) ? 1 : 2)` then a LOOP of separate `CreatureCmd.GainBlock` calls (EvilEye.cs:36-40) == `gains = 2 if ctx.combat.history.card_exhausted_this_turn() else 1` then a loop of separate `BlockCmd.apply` calls. Two SEPARATE gains rather than one doubled gain is load-bearing on both sides -- per-gain listeners (Juggernaut, and the Vambrace latch that creature_card_cmds G2 names Evil Eye as a witness for) fire twice. The condition matches too: `History.Entries.OfType<CardExhaustedEntry>().Any(e => e.HappenedThisTurn(CombatState) && e.Card.Owner == Owner)` (EvilEye.cs:25) == the sim's `history.card_exhausted_this_turn()`, with the owner clause folded into the single-player model. Presentation, folded in: TriggerAnim (34), the gaze VFX (35) and ShouldGlowGoldInternal (19).

OnUpgrade.rationale: `DynamicVars.Block.UpgradeValueBy(3m)` (EvilEye.cs:45) == `self._block += 3` (8 -> 11). The doubling condition is unchanged by the upgrade on both sides.

guards.what: the exhaust check is re-evaluated at play time, so a card exhausted EARLIER in the same turn counts but one exhausted by this card's own resolution cannot (EvilEye.cs:36)
guards.rationale: Both sides read the history once, before the first gain. Evil Eye exhausts nothing itself, so there is no self-interaction on either side.
